survivalGPU

Source: vignettes/survivalGPU.Rmd
survivalGPU.Rmd

survivalGPU performs survival analysis on GPU-accelerated hardware. Classical survival models don’t scale well to large datasets or to heavy bootstrap resampling on CPU: survivalGPU runs the core computations on the GPU to make both practical, while still working without one (CPU fallback).

Two models

  • coxphGPU(): Cox proportional hazards regression1 2, with the Efron or Breslow handling of ties. It takes the same inputs as survival::coxph()3, and its results work with the usual tools of the survival package (summary(), cox.zph(), survminer plots, …). See vignette("coxPH", package = "survivalGPU").
  • wceGPU(): Weighted Cumulative Exposure (WCE)4, which models how the effect of a time-varying exposure (e.g. a drug) depends on how long ago it was received, with a weight function estimated by splines. It takes the same inputs as WCE::WCE()5, and HR() computes hazard ratios between exposure profiles. See vignette("WCE", package = "survivalGPU").

Both models support bootstrap resampling, as a separate step after the fit: bootstrap() refits the model on many patient-level resamples of the data, processed in parallel batches (batchsize) on the GPU, to get bootstrap confidence intervals. For wceGPU(), several numbers of knots can be given (e.g. nknots = 1:3): the best one is selected by AIC or BIC, again in every bootstrap replicate, so that the confidence intervals also account for the uncertainty on this choice.

A first example 

library(reticulate)
use_virtualenv("survivalGPU") # the Python environment, see below

library(survivalGPU)
library(survival)

use_cuda() # TRUE if a GPU is detected, FALSE if survivalGPU runs on CPU

data <- lung
data$status <- data$status - 1 # event coded as 0/1
data$id <- seq_len(nrow(data))  # one row per patient

fit <- coxphGPU(Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex, data = data,
                x = TRUE, patient_id = "id") # both needed by bootstrap()
fit <- bootstrap(fit, R = 100)
summary(fit) # with bootstrap confidence intervals

How it works

survivalGPU is built on PyTorch (with KeOps additionally powering the WCE model). The R functions are thin wrappers around a Python implementation, called through the reticulate package: this Python code is bundled with the R package, but it needs a Python environment with PyTorch installed. vignette("installation", package = "survivalGPU") explains how to set it up.

The WCE model needs the pykeops Python package, which is not available natively on Windows: there, coxphGPU() works, and wceGPU() can be used through the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2).
